task.description:
REWORK (rework 2) -- design-level fix, not implementation. On branch feature/WF02-REQ263-20260906 (do not switch branches; ORCH will continue on it after this design lands), amend lib/letflow/design/req237-zig-provenance-marking-convention.md to add an explicit carve-out: closed/frozen docs/status/requirement_status*.yaml volumes are OUT OF SCOPE for the PROVENANCE-marking convention ENTIRELY, never to be touched, regardless of whether the edit is purely additive (a comment-only insertion still violates the frozen prefix).

BACKGROUND (independently verified by ORCH, not merely reported): docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml pins each closed volume's frozen_prefix_lines/frozen_prefix_sha256, enforced by test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs (assertion A6 among others). REQ-263's DOC-UPDATER commit (chunk 239i of this design's own section 6 chunking table) inserted 'PROVENANCE (historical, not current decision authority):' marker lines into 8 closed run-history volumes -- docs/status/requirement_status.yaml, .v2, .v3, .v4, .v5, .v6, .v7, and .v9 -- all landing inside their frozen prefixes. ORCH ran `mix test test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs` on this branch: 16/20 pass, 4 fail (all A6/frozen-prefix related). origin/main is confirmed unaffected -- this is entirely this branch's own defect.

ROOT CAUSE: this design document (your own prior output, section 6, the '239i' row of the REQ-239 chunking table, and the worked recommendation text at approx. line 395: 'docs/status/*, docs/frontend/*, docs/anti-patterns.md') recommended docs/status/* as a chunk WITHOUT ever checking whether any file under docs/status/ is a frozen/append-only artifact with its own competing invariant. The design's sections 1-5 (marker text, placement rules, unit shapes) never mention requirement_status.index.yaml or the frozen-prefix mechanism at all -- this is a genuine design gap, not an execution slip by DOC-UPDATER, who followed the design/requirement text as written.

YOUR TASK:
1. Add a new subsection (recommend under section 2, alongside the existing 'De-duplication' bullet, or as a new section 2.5 -- your call on placement, but it must be impossible for a future chunk owner to miss) stating plainly: before applying this convention to ANY file under docs/status/, check docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml's volumes: list. If the target file is a volume with status: closed, it is OUT OF SCOPE -- do not insert a marker anywhere within its frozen_prefix_lines, even as a comment-only/additive change, even if every other unit-shape rule in this design would otherwise apply cleanly. Only a volume with status: current (today, docs/status/requirement_status.v10.yaml) or a docs/status/ file that is NOT listed in the index's volumes: list at all (e.g. one-off release docs like docs/status/S1-release-2026-08-16.yaml) may be marked.
2. State the reasoning: the frozen-prefix mechanism (test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs assertion A6, sha256-pinned) is a competing invariant that pre-dates and outranks this convention for files under its scope -- this convention has no authority to modify a byte-frozen file, additive or not.
3. Separately assess: does REQ-263's OWN definition in docs/requirements.yaml need a scope correction? (Its acceptance_criteria currently list all 11 files in chunk 239i including the 8 closed volumes named above.) If yes -- and ORCH believes it does -- state the corrected file list explicitly for DOC-UPDATER to follow instead of the original text: the only files actually in scope are docs/status/S1-release-2026-08-16.yaml, docs/frontend/contract-gaps.md, and docs/anti-patterns.md (3 files, not 11). Frame this as a note DOC-UPDATER/ORCH can act on directly, not as a new requirement -- REQ-ANALYST/REQ-VALIDATOR are not being invoked for this narrow a correction per ORCH's own read of the sizing rule, but flag if you disagree.
4. Do NOT re-litigate or reopen anything else in this design (marker text, regex, other chunks' scope, REQ-237's own status) -- REQ-237 remains done. This is a narrow, additive amendment, dated 2026-09-06, in the same style as the two existing 2026-09-05 amendments at the top of the file.
5. Do not touch any code or docs/status/* files yourself -- design document only.
acceptance_criteria: lib/letflow/design/req237-zig-provenance-marking-convention.md has a new dated amendment (2026-09-06) at the top, in the same style as the existing two amendments, summarizing what changed and why

the design body itself (not just the top amendment note) states the frozen-volume carve-out as a mechanical, unambiguous rule referencing docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml's volumes:/status:/frozen_prefix_lines fields by name
the rule is stated to apply regardless of whether the edit is additive -- explicitly rules out the 'it's just a comment insertion' reading that produced this defect

the corrected REQ-263 file list (3 files: docs/status/S1-release-2026-08-16.yaml, docs/frontend/contract-gaps.md, docs/anti-patterns.md) is stated explicitly, with the 8 excluded closed volumes named and the reason (frozen, out of scope) given
no other section of the design is altered in meaning; REQ-237's status/scope is not reopened
no application code or docs/status/* files are touched by this handoff -- design doc only

requirement_text.REQ-263:
id: REQ-263
title: Apply the .zig provenance-marking convention to docs/status/*, docs/frontend/*, and docs/anti-patterns.md (closes ISS-0424 part 3c-10)
owner: DOC-UPDATER
status: pending
stage: S6
description: >
  Applies REQ-237's design decision (lib/letflow/design/req237-zig-provenance-marking-convention.md -- the PROVENANCE marker text and structural placement rule in section 2, the single-regex greppability justification in section 2(a), and the two worked before/after examples in section 4, including the REQ-231 cursor.zig worked example that lives inside docs/requirements.yaml itself) to this chunk of REQ-239's original scope, per that design's section 6 chunking recommendation: chunk 239i = docs/status/*, docs/frontend/*, and docs/anti-patterns.md.

  This is one of ten requirements replacing REQ-239 (deleted, too wide for one DOC-UPDATER turn at 58 non-requirements.yaml files plus 538 matching lines inside requirements.yaml): REQ-254 (239a) through REQ-263 (239i). Each sibling covers a disjoint scope; do not touch files or requirements.yaml entries outside docs/status/*, docs/frontend/*, and docs/anti-patterns.md under this requirement, even if they also carry a .zig citation -- they belong to a sibling chunk.

  Do NOT touch CLAUDE.md, README.md, or docs/migration/README.md's own already-completed Part 1 framing edits.

  MEASURED SCOPE AT DRAFT TIME (2026-09-05): 11 files in this chunk carry a .zig reference today: docs/status/requirement_status.v2.yaml, .v3, .v4, .v5, .v6, .v7, .v9, docs/status/requirement_status.yaml, docs/status/S1-release-2026-08-16.yaml, docs/frontend/contract-gaps.md, docs/anti-patterns.md.
acceptance_criteria: (named all 11 files above; see docs/requirements.yaml lines 15568-15573 for verbatim text)
depends_on: [REQ-237]
